name: Colourbox
label: 4AD
lede: Two brothers from London made one album of reggae, soul covers and sample-splattered noise for 4AD, then lent their drum machines to Pump Up the Volume, a UK No. 1 that started a sampling lawsuit before it reached the top.

eras.title: Dub, soul and samples on 4AD
eras.text: Brothers Martyn Young and Steven Young signed to 4AD and made dance tracks, dub and soul covers. The first line-up lasted one single.

years.h: The Young brothers start Colourbox in London
years.p: Martyn and Steven Young form the band with Ian Robbins and singer Debian Curry, and sign to 4AD.

years.h: The first single is Breakdown, with Curry singing
years.p: Breakdown backed with Tarantula is the band's debut on 4AD.

years.h: Lorita Grahame takes over the microphone
years.p: Curry and Robbins leave; [[Lorita Grahame|8ad1ebd6-d8ab-4240-91bd-e7ff2faf1fe1]] becomes the singer. Producer Mick Glossop reworks Breakdown for a reissue that still has Curry's vocal.

years.h: The first Colourbox record runs four tracks
years.p: The mini-album reaches No. 8 on the UK indie chart and shows off the band's experimental side.

years.h: Lorita Grahame sings Say You
years.p: It reaches No. 7 on the indie chart, with Fast Dump on the B-side. Punch follows in June and reaches No. 15.
years.xp: Electronic Sound's Ben Willmott traces it to U-Roy's Say You: a reggae cover from a band that also listened hard to Art of Noise and Cabaret Voltaire.

eras.title: One album, and a free one on top
eras.text: The only full-length Colourbox album went to No. 1 on the UK indie chart and came with a bonus LP for the first 10,000 buyers. It puts reggae and soul covers next to instrumentals built from samples and elegiac piano pieces.

years.h: A Supremes song on the back of The Moon Is Blue
years.p: The single reaches No. 3 on the indie chart, with a cover of You Keep Me Hangin' On as the B-side.

years.cap: Martyn and Steven Young with Lorita Grahame, c. 1985
years.src: Wikipedia: Colourbox (album) · Wikipedia: Colourbox · Electronic Sound: Colourbox (4AD, 1985)
years.h: Colourbox goes to No. 1 on the indie chart
years.p: The album mixes sample-heavy instrumentals, piano pieces, pop, reggae and soul. The first 10,000 copies come with a seven-track bonus LP.
years.xp:
Martyn Young produced it at four studios, including Palladium in Edinburgh and Guerilla in Crouch End. [[William Orbit|a7412cd0-e0b8-4fa1-8d24-75bb92a84946]] plays the guitar solo on Manic, Chris Karan adds tablas to Arena, and Just Give 'em Whiskey is an instrumental. [[Vaughan Oliver|2a1b1665-17fc-4ad2-9392-d6fe6788e96e]] designed the sleeve.

Willmott hears south London soundsystems in it as much as samplers: dub sub-bass, lovers rock and soul next to a solo piano piece and guitars cut with sci-fi and western samples.

years.src: Wikipedia: Colourbox · Discogs: The Official Colourbox World Cup Theme
years.h: Two singles in one day
years.p: Grahame sings Baby I Love You So, a No. 4 indie hit and No. 12 on NME's singles of 1986. The football-themed The Official Colourbox World Cup Theme comes out the same day and reaches No. 6.
years.xp: The World Cup single's B-side is a track called Philip Glass.

eras.title: Pump up the volume, then the lawyers
eras.text: Ivo Watts-Russell put Colourbox in a room, sort of, with A.R. Kane. The single built from other people's records went to No. 1 in Britain, went gold in the US, and helped make sampling a legal question. Colourbox never recorded under its own name again.

years.src: Wikipedia: Pump Up the Volume · Wikipedia: MARRS · Tone Glow 101: A.R. Kane
years.h: Ivo pairs Colourbox with A.R. Kane for one dance single
years.p: Both bands had told Watts-Russell they wanted to make a house record. Instead of working together, they cut separate tracks in separate studios and swapped parts.
years.xp:
The name M|A|R|R|S comes from initials: Martyn Young, Alex Ayuli, Rudy Tambala, Russell Smith of Terminal Cheesecake, and Steven Young. Colourbox built Pump Up the Volume; A.R. Kane built Anitina (The First Time I See She Dance), with Steve Young programming its drums. Producer John Fryer had the job of refereeing.

Colourbox told Watts-Russell they didn't want Anitina on the B-side and wanted Pump Up the Volume out as a Colourbox track. He said no, partly because Martyn Young's slow pace could have delayed it 12 to 18 months.

A.R. Kane had wanted Adrian Sherwood to produce. Rudy Tambala remembers Watts-Russell's answer: "No, I want you to work with Colourbox."

years.src: Wikipedia: Pump Up the Volume · Rolling Stone: How M/A/R/R/S' Pump Up the Volume became dance music's first pop hit
years.h: Pump Up the Volume takes its title from Eric B. & Rakim
years.p: The chant comes from I Know You Got Soul. DJs Dave Dorrell and C.J. Mackintosh scratch in more; the remix a week later, with Public Enemy and Bar-Kays samples, is the version that breaks.
years.xp: The idea traces back to Dave Dorrell's job cutting music for MTV Europe's launch bumpers, where the brief, he said, was "to put as many edits into 15 seconds as possible." The finished track lifts from James Brown, the Bar-Kays, the Last Poets, the Montana Sextet, Public Enemy, Wolfman Jack and a fire engine.

years.h: Stock Aitken Waterman get an injunction over a seven-second "hey"
years.p: Pete Waterman's phrase for sampling, in an open letter to the music press. The track was at No. 2 when SAW stopped distribution over a voice lifted from their hit Roadblock.
years.xp:
The sample was a distorted background moan with no melody in it. Dorrell later said he thought SAW would never have noticed if he hadn't mentioned it in a radio interview. Distribution halted for several days, and overseas pressings left it out.

The press pointed out that SAW's own Never Gonna Give You Up for Rick Astley, then climbing the same chart, borrowed the bassline of Colonel Abrams' Trapped. M|A|R|R|S couldn't afford a fight in court; the record went to No. 1 anyway.

years.src: Wikipedia: Pump Up the Volume · Rolling Stone: How M/A/R/R/S' Pump Up the Volume became dance music's first pop hit
years.h: Two weeks at No. 1 in Britain
years.p: Pump Up the Volume also tops the charts in Canada and New Zealand, reaches No. 13 on the Billboard Hot 100 and goes gold in the US.
years.xp: "We knocked Rick Astley off, who was the biggest thing in the country," Dorrell said, and the record held Michael Jackson off the top. The American release dropped the Roadblock samples. Martyn Young told Spin: "I think it's good that deejays are doing music."

years.src: Wikipedia: Pump Up the Volume · Wikipedia: MARRS · Wikipedia: Colourbox · Tone Glow 101: A.R. Kane
years.h: A.R. Kane want £100,000 for the M|A|R|R|S name
years.p: Colourbox wanted to keep using it and refused to pay. M|A|R|R|S had already said in September there would be no follow-up.
years.xp:
A.R. Kane said they were proud of the record but wouldn't do it again, and were unhappy their part of Pump Up the Volume nearly got cut. Wikipedia sums up the aftermath: sudden success and long litigation over samples meant Colourbox never recorded under its own name again.

Tambala's side, in 2023: Watts-Russell told A.R. Kane to give their royalties to Colourbox because Colourbox had been around longer, adding, "You need to be grateful." Tambala says he told him "fuck off," put the phone down and got a lawyer.

eras.title: A Grammy nod, a box set and a Tillmans show
eras.text: Martyn Young went on to produce other bands and kept the catalogue in order. The records came back as a best-of, a box set and, unexpectedly, an art exhibition.

years.h: Pump Up the Volume is nominated for a Grammy
years.p: The nomination is for Best Pop Instrumental Performance.

years.h: Martyn Young assembles Best of Colourbox 82/87
years.p: By then he had produced records for The Christians and [[The Wolfgang Press|84e4c923-0b83-49d3-9a89-a71a3339edcb]]. Grahame had sung on Hit the Roof's cover of Contact.

years.h: Four CDs for the 30th anniversary
years.p: 4AD's box set gathers the whole catalogue in an order chosen by Martyn Young.

years.cap: Colourbox: Music of the Group-1987) at Between Bridges, Berlin, 2014
years.h: Wolfgang Tillmans hangs Colourbox in a gallery
years.p: The photographer curates Music of the Band (1982–1987) at his Between Bridges space in Berlin, with a 16-track CD to go with it.

years.h: Founding member Ian Robbins dies
years.p: Robbins, who left in 1983, dies in 2014. No cause was given in the sources.

years.src: Wikipedia: Colourbox · Wikipedia: MARRS · Rolling Stone: How M/A/R/R/S' Pump Up the Volume became dance music's first pop hit
years.h: Steven Young dies
years.p: Martyn's brother and co-writer, who also programmed the drums on Anitina, dies on July 13, 2016.

years.h: The Tillmans compilation gets a double LP
years.p: It is reissued on vinyl to coincide with his Tate Modern exhibition.
